title: OSHA general industry bloodborne pathogens practice questions
description: Free OSHA bloodborne pathogens practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.1030. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: In 1910.1030, what does "parenteral" mean?

options.A: Contact of blood with intact skin
options.B: Piercing mucous membranes or the skin barrier, such as through needlesticks, human bites, cuts and abrasions
options.C: Swallowing food that was stored near blood specimens
options.D: Breathing air in a room where blood is drawn

questions.explanation: The rule defines parenteral as "piercing mucous membranes or the skin barrier through such events as needlesticks, human bites, cuts, and abrasions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the standard's definition of personal protective equipment, how are general work clothes such as uniforms that are not intended to protect against a hazard treated?

options.A: As PPE whenever the employer issues them
options.B: As PPE when worn in patient care areas
options.C: As PPE only if the employer launders them
options.D: As not being personal protective equipment

questions.explanation: General work clothes (e.g., uniforms, pants, shirts or blouses) "not intended to function as protection against a hazard are not considered to be personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: At a minimum, how often must the Exposure Control Plan be reviewed and updated?

options.A: At least annually, and whenever necessary to reflect new or modified tasks and procedures or new or revised positions with occupational exposure
options.B: Every three years
options.C: Every five years
options.D: Only when an OSHA compliance officer asks for it

questions.explanation: The plan "shall be reviewed and updated at least annually and whenever necessary" to reflect new or modified tasks and procedures which affect occupational exposure and new or revised employee positions with occupational exposure.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must the exposure determination treat the use of personal protective equipment?

options.A: It counts only exposure that remains after PPE is worn
options.B: It assumes every employee wears gloves at all times
options.C: It is made without regard to the use of PPE
options.D: It covers only employees who refuse to wear PPE

questions.explanation: The rule states: "This exposure determination shall be made without regard to the use of personal protective equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: Under the concept of Universal Precautions, how are all human blood and certain human body fluids treated?

options.A: As if known to be infectious for HIV, HBV and other bloodborne pathogens
options.B: As infectious only after the source individual tests positive
options.C: As non-infectious unless visibly contaminated with a sharp
options.D: As infectious only inside hospitals

questions.explanation: Under Universal Precautions, "all human blood and certain human body fluids are treated as if known to be infectious for HIV, HBV, and other bloodborne pathogens."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: Where the rule allows a contaminated needle to be recapped, how must the recapping be done?

options.A: With a two-handed technique while wearing gloves
options.B: By hand after the needle is bent
options.C: By any employee who has finished annual training, using both hands
options.D: With a mechanical device or a one-handed technique

questions.explanation: Such bending, recapping or needle removal "must be accomplished through the use of a mechanical device or a one-handed technique."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Universal precautions and work practice controls
questions.question: Which activity is prohibited in work areas where there is a reasonable likelihood of occupational exposure?

options.A: Washing hands with soap and water
options.B: Applying lip balm
options.C: Wearing disposable gloves
options.D: Reading the Exposure Control Plan

questions.explanation: "Eating, drinking, smoking, applying cosmetics or lip balm, and handling contact lenses are prohibited" in work areas where there is a reasonable likelihood of occupational exposure.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When is personal protective equipment considered "appropriate" under 1910.1030?

options.A: When it is the lowest-cost model available
options.B: When the employee picks it out personally
options.C: Only if it does not let blood or other potentially infectious materials pass through to or reach the employee's clothes, skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes under normal conditions of use, for as long as it will be used
options.D: When it is worn for no more than one hour

questions.explanation: PPE is appropriate "only if it does not permit blood or other potentially infectious materials to pass through to or reach" the employee's work clothes, street clothes, undergarments, skin, eyes, mouth, or other mucous membranes "under normal conditions of use and for the duration of time which the protective equipment will be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the rule say about washing disposable (single use) gloves so they can be used again?

options.A: They may be washed once if they are not torn
options.B: They may be decontaminated up to three times
options.C: They shall not be washed or decontaminated for re-use
options.D: They may be washed if the employee is allergic to other gloves

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Disposable (single use) gloves shall not be washed or decontaminated for re-use."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When must all personal protective equipment be removed?

options.A: Prior to leaving the work area
options.B: Only at the end of the work week
options.C: Only when it is visibly contaminated
options.D: Within 24 hours after the work is done

questions.explanation: "All personal protective equipment shall be removed prior to leaving the work area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must broken glassware that may be contaminated be cleaned up?

options.A: Picked up by hand, then hands washed right away
options.B: Left in place until the end of the shift
options.C: Wrapped in a towel and pressed together by hand
options.D: By mechanical means such as a brush and dust pan, tongs or forceps

questions.explanation: Broken glassware which may be contaminated "shall not be picked up directly with the hands" and "shall be cleaned up using mechanical means, such as a brush and dust pan, tongs, or forceps."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During use, how must containers for contaminated sharps be kept?

options.A: Laid on their side so sharps slide in easily
options.B: Maintained upright throughout use, replaced routinely and not allowed to overfill
options.C: Emptied by hand when full and put back in service
options.D: Stored in a locked room away from where sharps are used

questions.explanation: During use, sharps containers shall be easily accessible, "Maintained upright throughout use" and "Replaced routinely and not be allowed to overfill."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: For an employee with occupational exposure who has not had the vaccine, has not been found immune and has no medical contraindication, when must hepatitis B vaccination be made available?

options.A: Only after the employee's first exposure incident
options.B: After the employee has received the required training and within 10 working days of initial assignment
options.C: Within 90 days of initial assignment
options.D: Within one year of initial assignment

questions.explanation: Hepatitis B vaccination "shall be made available after the employee has received the training required in paragraph (g)(2)(vii)(I) and within 10 working days of initial assignment" to all employees who have occupational exposure, unless one of the listed exceptions applies.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: An employee signed the declination statement, but later, while still covered by the standard, decides to accept hepatitis B vaccination. What must the employer do?

options.A: Make hepatitis B vaccination available at that time
options.B: Refuse, because the declination was already signed
options.C: Make the employee wait until the next annual training
options.D: Charge the employee for the vaccine

questions.explanation: If the employee later decides to accept the vaccination while still covered under the standard, "the employer shall make available hepatitis B vaccination at that time."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure follow-up
questions.question: After a post-exposure evaluation, by when must the employer give the employee a copy of the evaluating healthcare professional's written opinion?

options.A: Within 30 days of the completion of the evaluation
options.B: Within 60 days of the exposure incident
options.C: At the next annual training session
options.D: Within 15 days of the completion of the evaluation

questions.explanation: The employer shall obtain and provide the employee with a copy of the written opinion "within 15 days of the completion of the evaluation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What color must the required warning labels be?

options.A: Bright green with white lettering
options.B: Black lettering on a plain white background
options.C: Fluorescent orange or orange-red, or predominantly so, with lettering and symbols in a contrasting color
options.D: Yellow with blue lettering

questions.explanation: The labels "shall be fluorescent orange or orange-red or predominantly so, with lettering and symbols in a contrasting color."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.1030, how must bloodborne pathogens training be provided to employees with occupational exposure?

options.A: At no cost to the employee and during working hours
options.B: On the employee's own time, unpaid
options.C: At the employee's cost, paid back after one year of employment
options.D: Outside working hours, as long as it is free

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Such training must be provided at no cost to the employee and during working hours."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Annual training for all employees must be provided within what period of their previous training?

options.A: Two years
options.B: Three years
options.C: Five years
options.D: One year

questions.explanation: "Annual training for all employees shall be provided within one year of their previous training."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For at least how long must the employer keep the medical records required by 1910.1030?

options.A: Three years from the date the record was made
options.B: The duration of employment only
options.C: The duration of employment plus 30 years
options.D: One year after employment ends

questions.explanation: The employer shall maintain the records required by paragraph (h) "for at least the duration of employment plus 30 years in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.1020."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.1030, Bloodborne pathogens (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long must bloodborne pathogens training records be kept?

options.A: Six months from the date of the training
options.B: 3 years from the date on which the training occurred
options.C: One year from the date of the training
options.D: Until the next training session

questions.explanation: "Training records shall be maintained for 3 years from the date on which the training occurred."
